messages.subject: Model Object Size
parts:
Hi Phil and MIRT Community,

I am wondering why the model object size can vary so much when you use different estimation methods. 

For example, the Small_Model (below) creates a 14,000 KB object; whereas when I change the method to MCEM, the Large_Model object becomes 530,000 KB.

Small_Model<- multipleGroup(df_transform,
                             model = model,
                             group = as.character(region),
                             rotate = "none",
                             invariance = c("slopes","intercepts","free_means"),
                             itemtype=item_type_list,
                             method = "QMCEM", 
                             technical=list(NCYCLES=20),
                             survey.weights=weight)

Large_Model<- multipleGroup(df_transform,
                             model = model,
                             group = as.character(region),
                             rotate = "none",
                             invariance = c("slopes","intercepts","free_means"),
                             itemtype=item_type_list,
                             method = "MCEM", 
                             technical=list(NCYCLES=20),
                             survey.weights=weight)

Thanks!
Leigh

Phil

messages.subject: Re: Model Object Size
parts:
Hi Leigh,

I'm having trouble reproducing this issue on my end with the latest mirt version. The objects appear to be of comparable size upon convergence with very minor deviation (too little to meaningfully spend time tracking down):

### 
data <- simdata(a=rep(1, 30), d= rnorm(30), N=10000, itemtype = '2PL')

mod1 <- mirt(data, 1)
mod2 <- mirt(data, 1, method = 'MCEM', technical = list(NCYCLES = 10))

object.size(mod1)
## 829024 bytes
object.size(mod2)
## 840984 bytes

group <- rep(c('G1', 'G2'), each = nrow(data)/2)

mod1 <- multipleGroup(data, 1, group=group)
mod2 <- multipleGroup(data, 1, group=group,  method = 'MCEM', technical = list(NCYCLES = 10))

object.size(mod1)
## 8823584 bytes
object.size(mod2)
## 8843080 bytes

Phil

On Fri, Sep 6, 2019 at 12:29 PM Phil Chalmers <rphilip....@gmail.com> wrote:
It's likely the case that additional objects are being stored needlessly in the returned object. I'll take a look to see what is causing the RAM increase.

Phil

Thanks for checking, Phil!

I tried a couple of things. I added survey weights and changed the item type. No big changes sizes there either.

###

data <- simdata(a=rep(1, 30), d= rnorm(30), N=10000, itemtype = '2PL')


mod1 <- mirt(data, 1)
mod2 <- mirt(data, 1, method = 'MCEM', technical = list(NCYCLES = 10))

mod3 <- mirt(data, 1, method = 'MCEM', technical = list(NCYCLES = 10) , survey.weights = runif(10000,0,1))

object.size(mod1)  
object.size(mod2)    
object.size(mod3)

mod4 <- multipleGroup(data, 1, group=group)
mod5 <- multipleGroup(data, 1, group=group, method = 'MCEM', technical = list(NCYCLES = 10))
mod7 <- multipleGroup(data , 1, group=group, method = 'MCEM', invariance = c("slopes","intercepts","free_means"), technical = list(NCYCLES = 10),survey.weights = runif(10000,0,1) ) 
 
object.size(mod4)   
object.size(mod5)     
object.size(mod6)     
#8647960 bytes
 

#Change the item type 
a <- matrix(rlnorm(20,.2,.3))
diffs <- t(apply(matrix(runif(20*4, .3, 1), 20), 1, cumsum)) 
diffs <- -(diffs - rowMeans(diffs)) 
d <- diffs + rnorm(20)  
dat <- simdata(a, d, 10000, itemtype = 'graded')   

group <- rep(c('G1', 'G2'), each = nrow(dat)/2)    

mod7 <- multipleGroup(dat, 1, group=group, technical = list(NCYCLES = 10), survey.weights = runif(10000,0,1) )  
object.size(mod7)   
#11113160 bytes

mod8 <- multipleGroup(dat, 1, group=group, method = 'MCEM', technical = list(NCYCLES = 10), survey.weights = runif(10000,0,1) )  
object.size(mod8)   
#11129448 bytes
